summary.headline: Shilpa Medicare Q4 FY26 revenue hit record INR439 crore (+30% YoY) with EBITDA INR121 crore (28% margin); FY26 revenue INR1,549 crore (+18%).
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR439 crore, up 30% YoY, with EBITDA of INR121 crore (+40% YoY, 28% margin). Full-year FY26 revenue was INR1,549 crore (+18%) and EBITDA INR445 crore (+30%, 29% margin), with gross margin at 70%. Adjusted PAT before exceptionals was INR87 crore for Q4 and INR232 crore for FY26 (about +135%). Q4 also included a INR30 crore exceptional gain from selling 31% of Sravathi Advance (JV now an associate, 34% held) and an INR18 crore associate share of profit tied to Maaia. Management gave no formal FY27 guidance, and most FY27 commentary was qualitative.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR985 crore, up 16%; Q4 revenue INR259 crore, up 16% YoY, driven by newly expanded capacity uptake and captive demand from formulations.

segments.name: Formulations (FDF)
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR205 crore, up 54% YoY; FY26 INR618 crore, up 30%. Excluding licensing income, base business grew 64% in Q4 and 75% for FY26. European formulation revenue exceeded INR200 crore, up over 100%.

segments.name: Biologics
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR150 crore, up roughly 100% YoY, driven by CDMO deal momentum; includes a prior-year-type milestone component (Orion albumin milestone referenced by analyst, not quantified).

segments.name: Licensing / service income
segments.commentary: Around INR200 crore per analyst question; management said licensing is lumpy but expects it to remain in a similar range at least in FY27.

guidance_outlook: No formal FY27 guidance; management said it does not provide guidance but expects the historical growth trajectory of 2-3 years to continue.
API expected to see steady growth in FY27; oncology API growth described as steady rather than steep.
Europe formulation expected to show healthy growth in FY27; Rotigotine Europe launch in FY27 with ramp-up mainly in FY28; Nilotinib generic competition impact expected mainly in FY28.
Biologics FY27 growth driven mainly by CDMO and biosimilar licensing (Europe, ROW); commercial revenue from Europe and ROW expected only from FY29; NorUDCA ROW revenue from FY28, Europe FY29.

EBITDA margin target of 35% described as ambitious and not immediate; interest outgo expected to stabilise at Q4 run-rate; capex to be funded broadly through internal accruals and FY27 capex not expected to grow significantly over FY26.
capex_capacity: Dedicated OLC manufacturing block commissioned in Q4 FY26; validation batches planned in Q1 FY27.
New oncology API block added to existing set-up; commissioning expected in FY27.
Dedicated peptide large-scale manufacturing block: equipment ordering completed; commissioning expected in FY27.
Building own ADC manufacturing suite (mAb, payload, linker, conjugation) planned as integrated capability in India.
Recombinant albumin: IMPD batches ongoing at new facility; IMPD submission planned in H1 FY27; India Phase III study approval already received from CDSCO.
demand_pricing: US formulation revenue rose from INR54 crore in FY25 to INR80 crore in FY26 but ran flat at about INR28 crore per quarter over the last 2-3 quarters; azacitidine generic was discontinued in the US.
NorUDCA launched in India in Nov 2025 (Q3); management cited steep QoQ growth and a healthy order book, but said a clearer volume picture would come around Q2 FY27 given the 6-month disease duration.
Oncology API is largely captive to own formulations; management stressed non-infringing API strength.
Raw material and solvent availability is fine, but prices have risen significantly.
CDMO API revenue about INR110 crore in FY26; biologics CDMO also significant; licensing income is pure product licensing with no CDMO element.

qa_highlights.question: Why has US formulation revenue stayed flat despite the US partner's share gains in Pemetrexed and Bortezomib?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said US revenue is rising and will continue to in FY27, but azacitidine generic was discontinued; focus is shifting to super-specialty products. Azacitidine FY25 revenue was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin rise toward 35% and will service/licensing income hold near INR200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said 35% is an ambitious target that will not be reached immediately because growth requires spending; licensing income is lumpy but expected to remain in a similar range at least.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the INR18 crore associate profit (Maaia) and is it recurring?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said Maaia (35% stake) had previously taken share of losses to zero the investment; improved performance reinstated the carrying value and share of profit was booked. Recurrence cannot be predicted.

qa_highlights.question: Europe FY27 growth and Nilotinib generic timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Generic Nilotinib competition expected in FY27 but tender contracts of 1-2 years mean limited value impact until FY28. Tadalafil ODF and Axitinib launches planned; CFO gave no growth guidance but expects healthy growth.

qa_highlights.question: Status of OLC PDUFA and FY27 contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Management does not project any meaningful OLC contribution in FY27; filing details are confidential.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the albumin IMPD submission pushed to H1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Batches for the IMPD are being produced at the new facility and must finish first; regulator review of a trial application typically takes 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the USFDA status at the Jadcherla site?
qa_highlights.answer: A USFDA audit observed issues; compliance was addressed and a re-audit is awaited. Management says US sales now come mainly from third-party CMOs, so there is no revenue impact.

risks_watch: Timing of OLC approval and launch, which management does not include in FY27 numbers.
Jadcherla USFDA re-audit outcome and pending tentative approvals; management says high-value TA products face late patent expiries.
NorUDCA volume trajectory, which management will only clarify around Q2 FY27.
Nilotinib generic entry in Europe in FY27/FY28 and the lumpy nature of licensing income.
Reinvestment needs versus margin expansion; raw material price inflation.
Sustainability of the Maaia associate profit, which management said it cannot predict.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the overall platform and growth trajectory, but cautious and evasive on specifics: management declined FY27 guidance, segment-level biologics and OLC numbers, and CDMO/biologics splits, deferring these to follow-up with IR.
key_quotes: For Shilpa Medicare, FY26 has been one such year where we have built our foundation.
We have seen steep growth on QoQ basis.
But obviously 35% is an ambitious target, which we would be working towards achieving.
So our major focus on U.S. will be from third-party CMO sites.
